scope.flow: GTL vault withdrawal queue: user calls queueWithdrawal to append a request to _queuedWithdrawal; admin processes batches or user cancels via _dequeue which loops over all queued withdrawals

statements.text: A user is able to queue as many withdrawals as he wants with any amount of shares he wants by calling queueWithdrawal.
A malicious user can submit withdrawal requests of a really small amount of shares (1 share).
The user calls queueWithdrawal, which puts a brand new withdrawal request into the _queuedWithdrawal array to be processed by the admin.
The malicious user spams the vault with many small-share withdrawal requests, all stored in _queuedWithdrawal, making the array expensive to loop over and maintain.
The attacker cancels his queued withdrawals by calling _dequeue with a withdrawal request id, which loops through all queued withdrawals checking for the matching id.

The issue occurs because there is no check on the input amount of shares, so a user can queue arbitrarily many withdrawals of arbitrarily small share amounts, growing _queuedWithdrawal so that looping over it (batch processing or _dequeue) can run out of gas and revert, DoSing the contract.
Queued withdrawal requests must be subject to a minimum amount of shares so that the number of queued withdrawals cannot be inflated by arbitrarily small requests.
A user must not be able to queue new withdrawal requests again before a required time interval has passed.
Processing and canceling queued withdrawals must be structured so that looping over the queue does not grow unbounded with the number of queued requests.
The attack costs the attacker nothing, so it can be repeated again and again.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether queueWithdrawal is permissionless for anyone or restricted; only that a user/malicious user can call it.
No explicit numeric bound or threshold for the minimum share amount or time interval is given.
Whether the DoS occurs during admin batch processing or during _dequeue cancellation is described as two alternative scenarios, not a single observed sequence.
The exact gas limit / number of requests needed to exhaust gas is not specified.
